about: EV charging-stop model for drive_plan.py (ev_charging.py). Car presets, Ontario DC fast network prices, consumption and charge-time factors. Usable kWh = evkx energy added 0 to 100%; f_10_80 = evkx average 10-80% power / peak DC power; highway and city kWh/100 km = NRCan ratings. nrcan_ref = the NRCan row behind the preset's figures (range and combined rating); drive_plan.py scales the battery of a looked-up EV whose NRCan range x rating implies a battery more than 10% smaller than the preset's (its energy x the preset's usable kWh / reference energy; the median of those ratios for an EV with no preset).

leaf-plus.name: Nissan LEAF PLUS 2019 to 2025 (62 kWh, CHAdeMO)

leaf-40.name: Nissan LEAF 2018 to 2025 (40 kWh, CHAdeMO)
leaf-40.notes: CHAdeMO only; 39 kWh usable of the 40 kWh pack. Charging curve assumed the same shape as leaf-plus (same 46 kW CHAdeMO hardware, no active battery cooling, slows on repeat fast charges). 2011 to 2017 LEAFs use this preset with their own 21 or 27 kWh battery
leaf-40.source: https://open.canada.ca/data/dataset/98f1a129-f628-4ce4-b24d-6f16bf24dd64 (NRCan 2020 to 2025 LEAF (40 kWh) and LEAF SV: 17.0 city, 21.2 hwy kWh/100 km, 240 km) ; curve shape from https://evkx.net/models/nissan/leaf/leaf_eplus_62_kwh/chargingcurve/

networks.name: Tesla Supercharger
networks.text: about $0.52 to $0.56/kWh peak, $0.28 to $0.30 off-peak (Tesla cars); congestion fee up to $0.50/min at busy sites above 80%

networks.name: Tesla Supercharger (non-Tesla car)
networks.text: about $0.43 to $0.81/kWh by time of day for non-Tesla cars; a membership of about $16.99/month gives the Tesla rate

networks.name: Electrify Canada
networks.text: $0.60 to $0.70/kWh by site; idle fee $0.40/min after 10 min

networks.name: FLO

networks.name: Petro-Canada
networks.text: about $0.27 to $0.33/min in 2026 guides, $0.50/min in 2022; no NACS plugs

networks.name: ChargePoint

networks.name: JULE

networks.name: other network

model.source: https://evkx.net/models/kia/ev9/ev9_long_range_awd/chargingcurve/ (charge curve method); trip-planner research, 2026-10-10; each factor below cites its own source

temp_factor.applies_to: highway and city consumption; 1/(1 - range loss)

winter_charge_time.note: cold battery without preconditioning charges slower; CAA saw about 28% added in 15 min in winter

model.charge_time: kwh / min(charger_kw * charger_limited_f, car_max_kw * f_10_80) * 60 + 5 min plug-in (x winter factor below 0 C); per-minute and per-hour prices bill the time without the 5 min plug-in allowance
model.level2_note: Level 2 hours = kWh / (min(site kW, 7.2) * 0.9); 0.9 is an assumed AC charging efficiency (onboard charger losses), not a measured figure
model.final_margin_note: the last stop adds 5 points over the reserve so arrival is not at the bare minimum

home_rate.text: home charging about $0.14/kWh all-in (OEB TOU off-peak 9.8 c/kWh plus delivery, regulatory and HST, less the 23.5% Ontario Electricity Rebate)

temp_normals_c.station: Toronto Lester B. Pearson Intl A, 1991 to 2020 Canadian Climate Normals (daily mean)

nlr.name: NLR (ex-NREL) Alternative Fuel Stations API, NRCan Canadian station data
nlr.rate_limit: DEMO_KEY about 10 calls per hour (observed header); free key from https://developer.nlr.gov/signup/ gives 1,000 per hour
